study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial
exposure: Antihypertensive treatment for mild chronic hypertension (BP goal <140/90 mm Hg)
Antihypertensive treatment for mild chronic hypertension (BP goal <160/105 mm Hg)
outcome: Unplanned maternal postpartum healthcare utilization (clinic visits, ED/triage visits, hospital admissions)
ED or triage/maternity evaluation unit visits
cohort: The study included 2293 pregnant patients with mild chronic hypertension who had a postpartum follow-up assessment.
finding: Treatment of mild chronic hypertension to a lower blood pressure goal (<140/90 mm Hg) was not significantly associated with overall unplanned postpartum healthcare utilization but was associated with lower rates of postpartum ED and triage visits.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with higher odds of unplanned postpartum healthcare utilization.
